title: Emergencies in the Board’s files, and how long each ran
question: Which emergencies did the Board of Supervisors declare or concur in since 2014, and over how long a period did it keep acting on each?
finding: The Board’s files since 2014 show 8 local emergencies that the Board concurred in or ratified. The coronavirus emergency runs through 39 Board files over 833 days (2020-02-25 to 2022-06-07); the next longest is Rim Fire (16 files over 427 days). Separately, the Board approved 50 emergency repairs or works declared by departments, with stated costs of $229.8 million; 12 of them, worth $75.8 million, date from 2023 or later. The middle case took 45 days from introduction to the Board’s vote, with the work already under way.
how: Board of Supervisors files from 2014 to November 2026 whose short title begins "Concurring in", "Emergency Declaration", "Emergency Contract" or "Emergency Work" and that passed or were filed. Motions concurring in a mayoral proclamation or ratifying a health officer’s declaration, and their later supplements, are grouped by the emergency named in the title; the span runs from the first file’s introduction to the last file’s passage. Each departmental emergency is one resolution; its cost is the amount stated in the title.
limits: The span is the period over which the Board acted, not the legal life of the emergency: titles do not carry the date a proclamation ended, and an emergency that began before 2014 (the Rim Fire) is cut off at the start. Declaring an emergency to repair a failed boiler, sea wall or water main is what Administrative Code section 6.60 provides for, and it requires the Board’s approval above $250,000. The Clerk’s proclamation records would supply the end dates. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).
